# NEAR: three layers, one token

> **NEAR isn't just an L1 anymore. It's a three-layer business, and the token is only beginning to capture that value.**

An investment thesis for the NEAR HACKATHON (Investment Thesis track), with data as of Nov 6, 2026. Every chart, with the query behind it, is on the [dashboard](DASHBOARD.md). How each number is computed is in [METHODS.md](METHODS.md). This is research, not investment advice.

The claim is the line above. The evidence for it runs through the next four sections, the evidence against it is under [Risks and considerations](#risks-and-considerations), and the results that would change our mind are in [the last table](#what-would-change-our-mind).

## Key points

- **Most of NEAR's money now comes from Intents, not the L1.** Intents earned 95% of NEAR's protocol revenue over Aug 2026–Oct 2026, against 34% a year earlier.
- **Intents is winning share.** It handled 58% of native cross-chain swap volume in Oct 2026, up from 45% a year earlier, while total DEX volume fell 56%.
- **NEAR AI is small but real.** It served 299.8B tokens on OpenRouter in the week to Nov 1, 2026, 21× its first full week, and customers have staked 1.4M NEAR to pay for it.
- **The token is beginning to capture that value.** Burns and buybacks offset 19.5% of new NEAR in 2026 Q3, up from 1.8% a year earlier. If Intents revenue keeps growing at a fading rate, they offset all of it by Jan 2029.

## The problem NEAR solves

Crypto is spread across hundreds of blockchains, each with its own assets and apps. Moving money between them usually takes several steps, a bridge, and a fee at each one. AI has a different problem: a few companies run the most capable models, and they see everything people send them.

NEAR has built a product for each problem. NEAR Intents turns a swap between any two chains into one step. NEAR AI runs AI models on hardware that keeps prompts private, even from NEAR AI. Both tie back to the NEAR token.

NEAR is still mostly judged as a base-layer blockchain (an L1), and on those numbers it looks like a network in decline: L1 transactions fell from 7.2M a day in Jan 2025 to 729.9K in Oct 2026. That view misses where the business went.

## NEAR's three layers

NEAR now works as three businesses, each built on the one below it.

**NEAR L1, the base chain.** The blockchain itself: accounts, smart contracts and payments, at an average fee of about 1 cent a transaction. Its own traffic has fallen, but more of what remains is Intents. In Oct 2026, 8.9% of L1 transactions went to the Intents contract, against 1.6% a year earlier.

**NEAR Intents, cross-chain swaps.** A user says what they have and what they want, competing market makers fill the order, and NEAR settles the result. In Oct 2026, Intents handled $3.99B of swaps, 2.3× its level a year earlier. On 1Click, the Intents channel with public swap-by-swap data, 269K users swapped through 352 apps, starting from 37 chains.

**NEAR AI, private AI.** NEAR AI Cloud runs open AI models inside secure hardware, so no one, not even NEAR AI, can read the prompts. Customers pay per use, or stake NEAR and receive AI credits. It is the newest layer. On OpenRouter, a marketplace for AI models, it served 299.8B tokens (units of text) in the week to Nov 1, 2026, 21× its first full week. Brave's AI assistant has run on it since Oct 15, 2026.

The layers are built to feed each other. AI agents need to pay and trade across chains, which is what Intents does, and every Intents swap settles on the L1.

The money has already moved. Intents produced 95% of NEAR's protocol revenue over Aug 2026–Oct 2026, against 34% a year earlier.

![NEAR protocol revenue by source, monthly](site/charts/c1-revenue.svg)

## Why the NEAR token has value

The token gains when NEAR is taken out of circulation, or locked up, faster than new NEAR is issued. Four mechanisms do that, and each one started or changed in the last 12 months.

- **Fees and burns.** Every L1 transaction pays a fee in NEAR. Until Nov 5, 2026, 30% of each L1 fee went to the contract being called and the rest was burned. Since then, all of it is burned.
- **Buybacks.** NEAR keeps a share of the fees on Intents swaps. Since Feb 23, 2026, that share buys NEAR on the market.
- **Staking.** NEAR is staked to secure the chain. Since Jul 30, 2026, holders can also stake with NEAR AI and receive AI credits. The NEAR stays locked while it is staked.
- **Less new supply.** On Oct 30, 2025, NEAR cut its cap on new issuance from 5% to 2.5% a year. A second cut, HSP-029, passed on Nov 2, 2026 and would lower it to 1.6% by Jan 2029.

![Follow the money: what each layer earned, and what reached the token](site/charts/money-flow.svg)

In Oct 2026, users paid $6.4M in fees on $3.99B of Intents swaps. NEAR kept $2.5M of that, worth 506.9K NEAR, which funds buybacks. L1 gas fees burned another 31.5K NEAR. Together that is 19.5% of the 2.8M NEAR issued in the month. NEAR AI's sales, an estimated $80K on OpenRouter, go to NEAR AI, and no published mechanism sends them to the token. What reaches the token from NEAR AI is staking, which locked 687.3K more NEAR.

**How much it adds up to.** Burns and buybacks offset 19.5% of the new NEAR issued in 2026 Q3, against 1.8% a year earlier. Counting NEAR newly staked with NEAR AI, the figure reached 43% in Aug 2026 and 44% in Oct 2026. Most new NEAR is still not offset, which is why we say the token is only beginning to capture the value.

![Share of new NEAR offset by burns and buybacks, monthly](site/charts/c6-ratio.svg)

**Where it could go.** Measured in NEAR, Intents revenue grew at a yearly rate of 115% between 2026 Q1 and 2026 Q3. If that growth halves every 2 years, burns and buybacks offset all new NEAR by Jan 2029. If it holds, they get there by Aug 2028. If revenue stops growing, they do not get there within the 6 years we project. Without HSP-029, the first of those dates moves to Apr 2030. These are projections from a short history, not forecasts. The assumptions are in [METHODS.md](METHODS.md#scenarios).

## NEAR in context

Intents is growing faster than its market. Among the venues that swap native assets between chains (Intents, THORChain, Chainflip and Maya), its share of volume rose from 45% to 58% over the year to Oct 2026. Its volume grew 131% in that time, while total DEX volume fell 56%.

|  | Oct 2026 | Oct 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Intents swap volume | $3.99B | $1.72B | 2.3× |
| NEAR's share of Intents fees | $2.5M | $295.8K | 8.4× |
| Distinct 1Click users | 269K | 132.6K | 2.0× |
| Apps sending swaps through 1Click | 352 | 48 | 7.3× |
| Intents share of native cross-chain swap volume | 58.3% | 44.5% | +13.8 pts |
| L1 transactions a day | 729.9K | 4.5M | −84% |
| NEAR staked with NEAR AI, month end | 1.4M | – | new |
| New NEAR issued | 2.8M | 5.2M | −47% |

> **Brave.** Brave's browser has over 128M monthly users. Since Oct 15, 2026, its AI assistant Leo offers GLM 5.3 Flash running on NEAR AI Cloud, so Leo users who pick that model get private AI they can verify. NEAR AI's homepage also names Venice, the Government of Bermuda and Abound as users of its private AI.

**Where NEAR stands today.** It is worth being direct about this. Intents is a working, growing business, and it already pays for buybacks. NEAR AI is early: it publishes no revenue, and we estimate its OpenRouter sales at about $1.4M a year. The token is earliest of all, because the mechanisms that send value to it have only just been switched on. The business has already moved beyond the L1 and the token has barely begun to reflect it, which is why our view is long-term bullish.

## Risks and considerations

This section is the evidence against the thesis, in one place.

- **Part of the shift is the L1 shrinking.** Intents' share rose partly because the rest of the L1 fell. One app, KaiChing, sent 65% of all L1 transactions in Mar 2026, and its stop caused 87% of the fall in Apr 2026. L1 fees are cheap by design, so a high Intents share of revenue is easy to reach.
- **Intents' activity is concentrated and led by trading.** On 1Click in Oct 2026, 74% of volume involved a stablecoin and one app (swapkit) routed 40% of it. Distinct users fell from 415.7K in Aug 2026 to 269K. Flow like this can leave as quickly as it came.
- **Market share is off its peak, and rivals are growing too.** Intents' share of native cross-chain swap volume peaked at 79% in Jun 2026 and was 58% in Oct 2026. Bridge aggregators grew 118% over the same twelve months, close to Intents' 131%. Our peer set leaves out large bridges whose data is paid, and wallets can switch routes cheaply.
- **NEAR AI is early and unproven.** It publishes no revenue. Our estimate from OpenRouter, one of its sales channels, is about $1.4M a year, and no published mechanism sends that money to the token. Staking for AI credits is concentrated: the largest staker holds 73% of the credits farm.
- **The token captures little so far.** In 2026 Q3, 80.5% of new NEAR was not offset. About 53% of the year's rise in the offset came from cutting issuance, not from more revenue. The NEAR bought back is held, not burned, and NEAR staked for AI can be withdrawn.
- **Governance and regulation.** Buybacks, the fee split and HSP-029 are governance decisions that can be changed or reversed, and HSP-029 still needs a protocol upgrade. Much of Intents' flow is stablecoins and privacy coins (Zcash was 14% of 1Click volume by origin in Oct 2026), so rules on cross-chain swaps or privacy assets could restrict it.

**What we couldn't measure.** NEAR AI publishes neither revenue nor total usage, so we see only its OpenRouter traffic and on-chain staking. Our user counts cover the 1Click channel only, about 27% of Intents volume in Oct 2026. Market share is against a peer set, not the whole cross-chain market. The full list is in [METHODS.md](METHODS.md#what-we-couldnt-compute).

## What would change our mind

The thesis rests on six claims. Each one has a result that would count against it, read from the same data and the same queries.

| What we claim | Where it stands | What would change our mind |
|---|---|---|
| [Most of NEAR's revenue now comes from beyond the L1](DASHBOARD.md#c1-revenue) | 95% of protocol revenue over Aug 2026–Oct 2026, against 34% a year earlier. | Intents' share of protocol revenue falling back below half. |
| [The L1 is becoming Intents' settlement layer](DASHBOARD.md#c2-l1-tx) | 8.9% of L1 transactions in Oct 2026, against 1.6% a year earlier. | Intents' share of L1 transactions no longer rising over a 12-month span. |
| [Intents is a real, broad-based growth engine](DASHBOARD.md#c3-volume) | $1.1B of 1Click volume and 269K users in Oct 2026, against $561.8M and 132.6K a year earlier; top 10 users at 15% of volume. | 1Click volume or users falling over a 12-month span, or the top 10 users' share of volume rising above half. |
| [Intents is gaining share, not just moving with the market](DASHBOARD.md#c4-share) | 58% of native cross-chain swap volume in Oct 2026, against 45% a year earlier. | Intents' share of native cross-chain swap volume falling over a 12-month span. |
| [NEAR AI is a working third layer](DASHBOARD.md#c5-tokens) | 299.8B tokens on OpenRouter in the week to Nov 1, 2026; 1.4M NEAR staked on Nov 5, 2026. | Weekly tokens on OpenRouter falling for a sustained period, or AI staking shrinking. |
| [The share of value reaching the token is rising](DASHBOARD.md#c6-flows) | 19.5% of new NEAR offset in 2026 Q3, against 1.8% a year earlier. | The share of new NEAR offset by burns and buybacks no longer rising, now that the fee switch is on. |
